ds: Missing-trader and carousel schemes exploit VAT refund and cross-border zero-rating rules by creating chains of invoices and trades where the VAT collected is never remitted. Common goods include electronics, metals, and emissions allowances; flows are fast, circular and between thinly capitalised companies.

src.t: Europol and EU bodies, public material on missing trader intra-community (MTIC) fraud
OECD, Technology Tools to Tackle Tax Evasion and Tax Fraud (2017)
FATF/OECD, Money Laundering Awareness Handbook for Tax Examiners and Tax Auditors (2012)
Council Directive 2006/112/EC on the common system of value added tax

rat: Missing-trader chains between thin companies with same-day circular flows of VAT-bearing payments.

ind.n: Newly formed company with rapid high-value cross-border trading
ind.cx: Company with minimal history, few staff and basic premises records large intra-EU or cross-border turnover quickly.
ind.fp: Fast-growing start-ups and trading vehicles exist.
ind.ds: A recently formed customer with little history or track record quickly records large turnover or trades in high-value or restricted goods.
ind.cn: Newly established customer with rapid high-value activity

ind.n: Circular payment flows among related counterparties
ind.cx: Funds return to origin after passing through several companies in a chain within days.
ind.fp: Group treasury or back-to-back trading may be similar.
ind.ds: Funds or goods-linked payments loop back to the originator or between related counterparties, or are traded back and forth.
ind.cn: Circular or round-trip flows among related parties

ind.n: Goods are high-value, low-weight and easily moved
ind.cx: Trade in mobile phones, chips, precious metals, or CO2 allowances with no storage or transport evidence.
ind.fp: These goods are legitimate high-volume trade lines.
ind.ds: Trade in mobile phones, chips, precious metals, or CO2 allowances with no storage or transport evidence.

ind.n: Payments in and out the same day with thin margin
ind.cx: Funds received from buyer are paid onward to supplier, often same day, leaving little retained.
ind.fp: Distributors and agents may operate on thin margins and pass-through.
ind.ds: Funds received from buyer are paid onward to supplier, often same day, leaving little retained.

ind.n: Payments to or from jurisdictions unrelated to goods
ind.cx: Counterparties are in different countries from the goods' origin or destination, often via third-country accounts.
ind.fp: Complex supply chains cause legitimate triangulation.
ind.ds: Payments, counterparties or sales originate in or go to countries with no link to the customer, declared business, services or goods.
ind.cn: Payments or activity in jurisdictions unrelated to the customer's business or goods

ind.n: Directors or addresses linked to prior defaulted VAT companies
ind.cx: Officers or premises previously appeared in VAT-defaulting entities or liquidations.
ind.fp: Directors can have genuine business failures.
ind.ds: Entities are repeatedly formed, abandoned or replaced by successors sharing directors, addresses or history of prior defaulted companies.
ind.cn: Short-lived or rotating entities with common controllers

ind.n: Invoices with identical formats across 'unrelated' suppliers
ind.cx: Documents share templates, wording or bank accounts across different companies.
ind.fp: Accounting software may produce similar templates.
ind.ds: Documents share templates, wording or bank accounts across different companies.

ind.n: Sudden stop of activity and withdrawal of funds before VAT due
ind.cx: Account activity ceases and balances drain just before VAT returns fall due.
ind.ds: Account activity ceases and balances drain just before VAT returns fall due.

ctl.ds: Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.

ctl.n: Tightened monitoring for new accounts and entities
ctl.ds: Applies lower thresholds and closer review during the first months of an account or entity and alerts on turnover far above onboarding projections. It addresses the elevated risk at the start of a relationship.

Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.

Investigates linked clusters and networks of accounts as one case, including broker networks and accounts connected to seizures or requests, rather than reviewing accounts individually. It disrupts organised activity that single-account review would miss.

Assigns each customer a risk tier from factors such as customer type, sector, geography, products and channel, which then drives the depth of due diligence and monitoring. Consistent scoring focuses resources on higher-risk relationships.

Verifies that goods physically moved as documented by matching shipping, container, customs and logistics records, and by requesting transport evidence such as delivery confirmations and warehouse records for sampled trades. It exposes fictitious or misdescribed shipments used to justify payments.
Reconciles cash, stock purchases, sales and exports with declared business activity to test whether deposits are plausible. It is used to identify unrecorded or injected cash.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

ctl.n: Duplicate document and duplicate financing detection
ctl.ds: Hashes and fuzzy-matches invoice and shipping documents within and across clients and checks shared registries so one asset cannot be financed twice. It detects reused and fabricated paper.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

Alerts when an inactive account abruptly resumes activity and requires identity re-verification and updated due diligence before reactivation. Dormant accounts are attractive for takeover and for passing illicit funds.

ctl.n: Law enforcement request handling and liaison
ctl.ds: Handles law-enforcement, tax-authority and customs requests promptly, reviews related accounts and maintains rapid contact points. It supports investigations and asset recovery while keeping responses consistent.
